107196: Dennis O’Neil and Dick Giordano’s The Man Who Falls, following Bruce Wayne’s travels and training before he becomes Batman, alongside other DC origin stories. A placeholder until I find the edition I remember.
192979: Darwyn Cooke and Tim Sale tell Superman’s first encounter with kryptonite, early in his career. Collects Superman Confidential #1–5 and #11, with a Sale sketchbook and an introduction by Cooke.
358525: Geoff Johns and David Goyer reintroduce the Justice Society, DC’s first super team, mixing its older heroes with a new generation. Collects JSA #1–25, JSA All Stars #1–8 and related specials. The start of a longer run.
381368: Geoff Johns, Ethan Van Sciver and Ivan Reis return Hal Jordan to life in Rebirth, then build to the Sinestro Corps War. First of my three Johns omnibuses; Vol. 2 is next.
394254: Kevin Eastman and Tom Waltz give the Turtles a new origin in IDW’s ongoing series, the start of the complete run in reading order. Collects Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #1–12 and the five Micro-Series one-shots.
400438: Geoff Johns, Ivan Reis and Doug Mahnke take Hal Jordan from his retold origin and the Red Lanterns to Blackest Night, where the dead return as Black Lanterns. The middle of my three volumes.
422214: Kurt Busiek and Stuart Immonen follow a young Clark Kent in the real world, teased for sharing Superman’s name, until he discovers he really can fly. Collects Superman: Secret Identity #1–4; it stands on its own.
427280: Geoff Johns and Doug Mahnke close the run: the Brightest Day issues, then Green Lantern (2011) #1–20, with Sinestro back in a green ring and Hal without one. Read after Vol. 2.
444953: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli follow Bruce Wayne and Jim Gordon’s first year in Gotham, in two slipcased volumes: recolored and original 1987 versions. I’ve read it in DC Finest and want this edition.
466699: Doug Moench, Chuck Dixon, Jim Aparo and others tell how Bane frees Arkham, wears Batman down and breaks his back, leaving Jean-Paul Valley in the cowl. Vol. 2 continues the story.
470667: Darwyn Cooke’s Batman: Ego, where Bruce confronts the Batman inside him, plus the Catwoman heist Selina’s Big Score and short stories. Most of it is also in the Absolute Edition I have on order.
477616: Ta-Nehisi Coates, Brian Stelfreeze and Chris Sprouse set T’Challa against an uprising in Wakanda led by Tetu and Zenzi. Collects Black Panther (2016) #1–12, the complete A Nation Under Our Feet.
525077: Grant Morrison with Andy Kubert, J.H. Williams III and Tony Daniel: Batman meets his son Damian and battles the Black Glove through Batman R.I.P. First of three volumes, all on my wishlist.
539080: Mark Waid and Alex Ross bring the Justice League back to face a new generation of heroes who have become as reckless and violent as the villains they fight. Collects Kingdom Come #1–4 at Absolute size.
549725: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale’s Batman in one volume: the Haunted Knight specials, The Long Halloween’s year of holiday murders, its sequel Dark Victory, and Catwoman: When in Rome.
582586: Kurt Busiek and Alex Ross show the Marvel Universe from 1939 to the death of Gwen Stacy through the eyes of news photographer Phil Sheldon. Collects Marvels #0–4; I’ve read it.
595563: Geoff Johns and Ivan Reis relaunch Aquaman for the New 52, facing the Trench and Black Manta, then Atlantis itself in Throne of Atlantis. Collects Johns’s whole Aquaman (2011) run plus Justice League #15–17.
595565: Grant Morrison with Frank Quitely and others: Dick Grayson becomes Batman with Damian as Robin while Bruce fights his way back through time. Read after Vol. 1; Vol. 3 finishes the run.
615732: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo’s New 52 Batman, from the Court of Owls and Death of the Family to Zero Year’s retold origin. Collects the first 33 issues; Vol. 2 finishes the run.
621282: Greg Pak and John Romita Jr. bring the Hulk back from Sakaar for revenge on Iron Man, Reed Richards, Doctor Strange and Black Bolt. Just World War Hulk #1–5, no tie-ins. Read after Planet Hulk.
629057: Brian Michael Bendis and Alex Maleev turn Daredevil into a crime story: a newspaper outs Matt Murdock, and he ends up declaring himself the Kingpin of Hell’s Kitchen. Vol. 2 finishes their run.
629058: Brian Michael Bendis and Alex Maleev’s second half, Daredevil #61–81, ending with The Murdock Papers and Matt Murdock’s arrest by the FBI. Read after Vol. 1; this finishes their run.
629060: Peter David starts his Hulk run with Todd McFarlane, Jeff Purves and others: the gray Hulk, the Leader’s revival and Joe Fixit in Las Vegas. Collects Incredible Hulk #328 and #331–368 with crossovers.
634520: Jonathan Hickman, Pepe Larraz and R.B. Silva build a mutant nation on Krakoa and rewrite X-Men history across two six-issue series. My reading order follows the book’s alternating issues.
634654: Geoff Johns and Gary Frank retell Superman’s beginnings, from Smallville and the Legion to Metropolis, Lois Lane and Lex Luthor. Collects Superman: Secret Origin #1–6. A different version from Birthright, which I own.
634655: Jeph Loeb, Ed McGuinness and Michael Turner start the series with President Luthor’s manhunt for Superman and Kara Zor-El’s arrival as Supergirl. Collects Superman/Batman #1–43 and both Annuals.
643956: Mike Grell writes and draws The Longbow Hunters, moving Oliver Queen to Seattle and dropping the trick arrows, then writes Green Arrow #1–50. My planned starting point for Grell’s run.
644056: Chris Claremont, Frank Miller, John Buscema and others: Wolverine’s Hulk debut, his Japan miniseries and the start of his 1988 series. Its Weapon X chapters overlap my deluxe edition.
648707: Geoff Johns and Scott Kolins’s Wally West: a powerless Flash trapped in a mirror Keystone City, and a cult killing everyone he has rescued. Collects The Flash #164–191 and related specials. Read after the Waid volumes.
648796: Chris Claremont’s X-Men with Dave Cockrum and John Byrne, from the new team’s debut in Giant-Size X-Men #1 to the start of the Dark Phoenix Saga. Where I want to begin the run.
652480: Grant Morrison and Dave McKean send Batman into Arkham Asylum after the inmates take it over, cutting between his night there and the history of founder Amadeus Arkham. On my wishlist.
652482: Dennis O’Neil, Neal Adams and others introduce Talia and her father Ra’s al Ghul, including the story Daughter of the Demon. These stories come before my Demon Trilogy.
661339: Grant Morrison, Chris Burnham and Yanick Paquette’s Batman Incorporated, with Bruce backing Batmen around the world against the criminal network Leviathan. Read after Vol. 2; this finishes Morrison’s run.
671692: Chris Claremont with Dave Cockrum, Paul Smith, Brent Anderson and Frank Miller: the Brood Saga, God Loves, Man Kills, the Wolverine miniseries and Rogue joining the team. Read after Vol. 2.
685970: Chuck Dixon, Alan Grant and others shake Gotham with the Cataclysm earthquake and follow the city until the government cuts it off. Comes before No Man’s Land Vol. 1 in my reading order.
685972: Grant Morrison and Howard Porter relaunch the Justice League around DC’s seven biggest heroes, facing White Martians, Prometheus and Mageddon. Includes JLA: Earth 2 with Frank Quitely and JLA One Million.
692148: Ed Brubaker and Doug Mahnke retell Batman’s first case against the Joker, set right after Year One. Also collects Brubaker’s Detective Comics #784–786 team-up with Alan Scott and Gotham Noir with Sean Phillips.
700430: Ed Brubaker and Steve Epting bring Bucky back as the Winter Soldier and build to Steve Rogers’s death in #25. Collects Captain America (2005) #1–25 and two one-shots.
706357: James Tynion IV, Eddy Barrows, Álvaro Martínez and others have Batman and Batwoman train Red Robin, Spoiler, Orphan and Clayface as a team. Collects Detective Comics #934–981.
713236: Roger Stern’s 1980s Spider-Man with John Romita Jr. and others: the Hobgoblin’s debut, The Kid Who Collects Spider-Man and fights with the Juggernaut and Kingpin. Collects Spectacular #43–61 and #85, Amazing #206 and #224–252 and Annuals #16–17.
728937: Jim Starlin and Jim Aparo’s Jason Todd story, where a reader vote decides his fate at the Joker’s hands, plus A Lonely Place of Dying, with Tim Drake’s arrival. Under the Red Hood follows.
728944: Ra’s al Ghul takes out the JLA one by one using Batman’s own plans for stopping his teammates, plus an Adam Strange space mission. Collects JLA #18–21, #32–33 and #43–46 and two JLA Secret Files #3 stories.
737375: Peter J. Tomasi and Patrick Gleason’s Rebirth Superman follows Clark and Lois raising their son Jon, through Son of Superman and Super Sons of Tomorrow. Their Batman and Robin omnibus is on my wishlist.
737376: Tom King and Andy Kubert send Superman across the galaxy after a girl abducted from Metropolis, testing how far he will go for one person. Read, no longer on my shelf.
764502: Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley restart Spider-Man with a high-school Peter Parker, from the spider bite to fights with the Green Goblin, Doctor Octopus and Venom. Covers #1–39; Vol. 2 is next.
770779: Jonathan Hickman, Dale Eaglesham and Steve Epting start with Reed’s council of alternate selves and build to the death that ends the Fantastic Four and starts the Future Foundation. Vol. 2 is next.
772235: Bob Gale, Greg Rucka and others start No Man’s Land, with a quake-ruined Gotham cut off and carved up by gangs. Read after Road to No Man’s Land; Vol. 2 is on my wishlist.
777644: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo finish their run with Endgame and Superheavy, where Jim Gordon becomes Batman, plus their later Batman: Last Knight on Earth. Collects Batman #34–52; read after Vol. 1.
783486: Jonathan Hickman, Steve Epting and others finish the run: Johnny Storm returns, Galactus arrives and Valeria enlists Doctor Doom against the Council of Reeds. Read after Vol. 1, before Hickman’s Avengers.
790998: Jason Aaron, Esad Ribić and Russell Dauterman pit three Thors against Gorr the God Butcher, then hand the hammer to a new Thor when Odinson proves unworthy.
791804: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely follow Superman through what may be his final year after a Lex Luthor plot overloads him with solar radiation. Collects All-Star Superman #1–12 with extras.
800436: Jonathan Hickman with Jerome Opeña, Steve Epting and others: the Avengers expand, the Illuminati secretly fight colliding universes, and Thanos invades in Infinity. Read after Hickman’s Fantastic Four; Vol. 2 is next.
806058: Mattson Tomlin and Andrea Sorrentino set an early-career Batman against a copycat who murders criminals on camera, turning Gotham’s police and elite against him. The complete three-issue story.
815436: Peter David, Archie Goodwin, John Byrne and others continue Wolverine’s 1988 series, from the Gehenna Stone in Madripoor to the Lazarus Project. Read after Vol. 1; I want the Jim Lee cover.
816377: Ed Brubaker, Greg Rucka, Michael Lark and others follow the GCPD, including Renee Montoya, Maggie Sawyer and Harvey Bullock, as they work Gotham’s cases and clean up after Batman. Collects Gotham Central #1–40, the complete series.
816383: Dennis O’Neil and Denys Cowan follow reporter Vic Sage, who as the faceless Question digs into Hub City’s corruption. Collects The Question #1–27 and the Question, Green Arrow and Detective Comics Annuals #1. Vol. 2 continues the run.
820223: Donny Cates and Ryan Stegman tie Venom to Knull, the ancient god of the symbiotes, building through Absolute Carnage to King in Black. Collects Venom (2018) #1–35 and both events.
832902: Alex Ross writes and paints the Fantastic Four’s trip into the Negative Zone, picking up threads from a 1960s Lee and Kirby story. Read, no longer on my shelf.
833426: Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley continue with the Black Cat, a Hollywood detour, the Ultimate Six and Carnage. Collects #40–71 and Ultimate Six #1–7; Vol. 3 is on my wishlist.
847836: Geoff Johns and Gary Frank reimagine Batman’s origin, with a young Bruce Wayne hunting his parents’ real killers and the corrupt police who let them go. Collects all three Earth One graphic novels.
847839: Chuck Dixon, Greg Rucka, Dennis O’Neil and others finish No Man’s Land, with Lex Luthor offering to rebuild Gotham on his own terms. On my wishlist to finish the No Man’s Land run.
860093: Peter David and Dale Keown continue the run: Doc Samson helps the Hulk pull his personalities together, the Pantheon recruits him and the Leader returns. Collects Incredible Hulk #369–400, Annuals #16–18 and X-Factor #76. Read after Vol. 1.
861150: Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee run Batman through most of his rogues while a bandaged stranger called Hush pulls the strings. Collects Batman #608–619 and the Wizard #0 interlude, with anniversary extras.
861164: Mark Waid and Greg LaRocque begin the Wally West run with Born to Run, his Kid Flash origin, and The Return of Barry Allen. Collects The Flash #62–91; Vol. 2 is next.
861168: George Pérez rebuilds Wonder Woman after Crisis on Infinite Earths, sending Diana from Themyscira to stop Ares and bringing in Cheetah and Silver Swan. Collects Wonder Woman (1987) #1–24 and Annual #1.
863414: Mark Waid and Leinil Francis Yu retell Superman’s origin, from Clark reporting in Africa to his first conflict with Lex Luthor in Metropolis. Collects the twelve-issue series with an afterword by Waid.
891648: Jonathan Hickman with Mike Deodato and others: universes keep colliding, the Avengers turn on the Illuminati, and Time Runs Out leads into Secret Wars, which is on my wishlist. Read after Vol. 1.
891650: Greg Pak and Carlo Pagulayan’s Hulk, shot into space by the Illuminati, fights his way from gladiator to rebel on the planet Sakaar. I’m reading it now; World War Hulk follows.
891652: David Michelinie, Todd McFarlane, Erik Larsen, Mark Bagley and others chart Venom’s early years, from Amazing Spider-Man #300 to the Maximum Carnage crossover. Gathers his appearances across the Spider-Man titles.
904696: Peter J. Tomasi and Patrick Gleason follow Bruce Wayne as he tries to raise his assassin-trained son Damian as Robin. On my wishlist to sit beside their Superman omnibus.
921601: Kelly Sue DeConnick, Phil Jimenez, Gene Ha and Nicola Scott tell how the Olympian goddesses founded the Amazons and how Hippolyta’s arrival led to war across heaven and Earth. Collects #1–3 in one oversized hardcover.
931967: Daniel Warren Johnson follows Lona Steelrose, a would-be pro wrestler living in her mother’s shadow, after a wrestling-obsessed necromancer invites her into a dangerous tournament. Collects Do a Powerbomb! #1–7.
932038: Al Ewing and Joe Bennett turn the Hulk into a horror series: Bruce Banner cannot stay dead, and every death brings the Hulk back. Collects the full run, Immortal Hulk #0–50, with related issues.
932048: Barry Windsor-Smith writes and draws Logan’s capture by a secret Canadian military project that bonds adamantium to his skeleton, told as lab horror. Restored from Marvel Comics Presents #72–84; I’ve read it.
935895: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale follow Clark Kent through four seasons as he leaves Smallville and becomes Superman in Metropolis. Collects Superman for All Seasons #1–4 with related short stories and extras.
958547: Peter J. Tomasi, Patrick Gleason, Dave Gibbons and others follow Guy Gardner, Kyle Rayner and the wider Corps, from Recharge onward. Collects Green Lantern Corps #1–3 and #7–38 with related issues. Overlaps my Johns omnibuses in places.
959381: Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley’s last stretch together, with Peter dating Kitty Pryde and the Ultimate Clone Saga. Collects #72–111; read after Vols. 1 and 2, which I own.
959415: Ryan North and Iban Coello scatter the Fantastic Four after a disaster in New York, leaving them to odd trouble like a time loop and a town of Doombots. Read, no longer on my shelf.
985271: Judd Winick and Doug Mahnke bring Jason Todd back as the Red Hood to take over Gotham’s drug trade and confront Batman. Includes Red Hood: The Lost Days; read after A Death in the Family.
990793: Peter J. Tomasi, Patrick Gleason, Jorge Jimenez and others team up Jon Kent and Damian Wayne. Collects Super Sons #1–16, Adventures of the Super Sons #1–12 and Challenge of the Super Sons #1–7. Some chapters overlap my Superman omnibus.
1012710: Walter Simonson’s Thor, with Beta Ray Bill, Surtur, the death of Odin and Thor turned into a frog. Collects Thor #337–355, #357–369 and #371–382 and Balder the Brave #1–4, recolored by Steve Oliff.
1017824: Greg Pak and John Romita Jr. bring the Hulk back from Sakaar for revenge on the Illuminati who exiled him, with the tie-ins and aftermath. Next after Planet Hulk, which I’m reading now.
1025733: Frank Miller and John Romita Jr. retell Matt Murdock’s origin, from the accident that blinds him and his training under Stick to his first moves against the Kingpin. Read, no longer on my shelf.
1026827: Scott Snyder, Jock and Francesco Francavilla put Dick Grayson in the cowl against a string of murders and Jim Gordon’s estranged son. Comes before Snyder’s New 52 run with Capullo.
1035965: Brian Michael Bendis with Stuart Immonen and David Lafuente: the Green Goblin escapes, Venom fights Carnage and Ultimatum floods Manhattan. Collects #112–133, Annual #3, Ultimatum: Spider-Man Requiem #1–2 and the 2009 series #1–15. Read after Vol. 3.
1047078: Tom King and Bilquis Evely send Kara Zor-El across space after an alien seeking revenge comes looking for her. Collects Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow #1–8, with an unpublished alternate script for #6 and Evely’s behind-the-scenes art.
1052882: Chris Claremont and John Byrne finish the Dark Phoenix Saga and tell Days of Future Past before Dave Cockrum returns. Read after Vol. 1; I’m still looking for a copy.
1062985: Paul Dini and Alex Ross’s six painted stories, from Superman: Peace on Earth to Justice League: Liberty and Justice. Most set the heroes against real-world problems like hunger and crime.
1067105: Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribić end the multiverse and rebuild it as Battleworld under God Emperor Doom. Follows my Avengers Vol. 2, though it reprints the Time Runs Out issues I already have.
1067621: Jim Starlin and Bernie Wrightson pit Batman against Deacon Blackfire, a cult leader who builds an army from Gotham’s homeless and brainwashes him in captivity. Collects #1–4 with a Wrightson art gallery.
1067622: Peter David with Jim Calafiore, Martin Egeland, Phil Jimenez and others: Aquaman loses his kingdom, family and hand, then fights to reclaim his throne. Collects Aquaman (1994) #0–49, Annuals #1–4, Time and Tide #1–4 and Tempest #1–4.
1067636: Mark Waid with Mike Wieringo, Salvador Larroca and others: Impulse arrives, Wally glimpses a grim future, and Savitar hunts speedsters in Dead Heat. Collects The Flash #0 and #92–129; Morrison and Millar’s volume follows.
1074026: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli’s Year One, plus Mike W. Barr, Alan Davis and Todd McFarlane’s Year Two against the Reaper, in a DC Finest collection. Read, no longer on my shelf.
1081038: Greg Rucka, Ed Brubaker, Scott McDaniel and others jail Bruce Wayne for Vesper Fairchild’s murder, then send him on the run while the Bat-family hunts the real killer. Both crossovers, in reading order.
1091823: Jason Aaron, Ron Garney and others pit Wolverine against Mystique, kung-fu gangsters and Roxxon’s adamantium-enhanced soldiers. Its Weapon X issues are the 2009 series, not Barry Windsor-Smith’s story.
1094572: Grant Morrison and Mark Millar’s run on Wally West’s Flash, drawn by Paul Ryan and others: The Flash #130–141 plus related stories. Read after Waid Vol. 2; Waid Vol. 3 picks up after it.
1101016: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale have Matt Murdock write to the late Karen Page about his first days as Daredevil in the yellow costume. Read, no longer on my shelf.
1115275: Daniel Warren Johnson, Jorge Corona and Mike Spicer start the Energon Universe Transformers, with the Autobots and Decepticons renewing their war on Earth and Optimus Prime as humanity’s only hope. Collects Transformers #1–12.
1121691: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale have Peter Parker look back on falling in love with Gwen Stacy, just as Mary Jane enters his life. Collects Spider-Man: Blue #1–6.
1124015: Phillip Kennedy Johnson, Daniel Sampere, Riccardo Federici and others send Superman to Warworld to free its people from Mongul. Collects the Warworld saga in reading order with Superman and the Authority #1–4. Vol. 1 of Johnson’s run.
1124152: Greg Rucka writes Diana as an ambassador as well as a fighter, amid mythology and politics. Collects Wonder Woman #195–226, The Hiketeia and Blackest Night: Wonder Woman #1–3, with crossover issues. Separate from his Rebirth run.
1132914: Tom Taylor and Bruno Redondo return Dick Grayson to Blüdhaven, with Barbara Gordon and his wider family around him. Collects Nightwing #78–96, the 2021 Annual and Superman: Son of Kal-El #9. First of two volumes.
1137092: Kelly Thompson and Hayden Sherman reimagine Diana as an Amazon raised in the underworld by Circe, fighting for the surface world with weapons forged in Hell. Collects Absolute Wonder Woman #1–7.
1137100: Jason Aaron and Rafa Sandoval rebuild Superman as a Kryptonian survivor who takes on the Lazarus Corporation and its Peacemaker soldiers. Collects Absolute Superman #1–6.
1143870: Mike W. Barr and Dennis O’Neil’s Ra’s al Ghul graphic novels Son, Bride and Birth of the Demon, drawn by Jerry Bingham, Tom Grindberg and Norm Breyfogle. Tales of the Demon is on my wishlist.
1143890: Darwyn Cooke writes and draws DC’s heroes from the end of World War II to the founding of the Justice League. Collects the six-issue series, its Justice League special and a Solo #5 story.
1148976: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale return to the Hulk’s first days, when he was gray, and Bruce Banner’s love for Betty Ross. Collects Hulk: Gray #1–6; I’ve read it.
1161732: Deniz Camp and Javier Rodríguez follow FBI agent John Jones after an alien mind calling itself the Martian settles into his head. Collects Absolute Martian Manhunter #1–6.
1162745: Mark Waid and Chris Samnee tell Dick Grayson’s first year as Robin, with a crime boss called the General at war with Gotham’s mob families. Collects the twelve-issue series.
1162844: Darwyn Cooke’s Batman and Catwoman stories at Absolute size, including Ego, Selina’s Big Score, Catwoman #1–4 and Batman/The Spirit. On order for October 20, 2026; it overlaps my Ego and Other Tails deluxe.
1170454: Robert Kirkman, Cory Walker and Ryan Ottley follow Mark Grayson as he gets his powers and learns what his father, Omni-Man, really is. Collects Invincible #0–47 and the Spider-Man team-up from Marvel Team-Up #14.
1170502: Mark Waid, Brian Augustyn and Paul Pelletier finish the Wally West run, which brings in a Dark Flash from a parallel world. Read after the Morrison and Millar volume.
1184534: Dan Watters and Hayden Sherman tell four self-contained, three-part detective cases from Batman’s early years, kept to street-level crime. Collects the complete series.
1189328: Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino set Oliver Queen against Komodo, a rival archer, as secrets about his past and his late father surface. Includes The Outsiders War; collects Green Arrow (2011) #17–34 and #23.1.
1190506: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale have Steve Rogers look back on World War II and his partnership with Bucky Barnes. Read, no longer on my shelf.
1195681: Mark Waid and Dan Mora team up Batman and Superman in adventures set early in their careers, with Dick Grayson as Robin. Collects #1–11 and a Detective Comics #1050 story.
1202954: Chip Zdarsky’s Spider-Man, including Life Story with Mark Bagley, where Peter ages in real time, and Spider’s Shadow, where he keeps the symbiote suit. Collects Spectacular Spider-Man #1–6 and #297–310, Life Story #1–6 and Spider’s Shadow #1–5.
1216560: Greg Rucka, Nicola Scott and Liam Sharp bring Diana into the Rebirth era, telling Wonder Woman: Year One alongside a present-day story. Collects Wonder Woman (2016) #1–25, Rebirth #1 and Rucka stories from four specials.
x-batman-legends-of-the-dark-knight-omni: Dennis O’Neil, Grant Morrison, Doug Moench and others tell self-contained stories from Batman’s early years, beginning with the Shaman, Gothic and Prey arcs. On order; currently scheduled for June 1, 2027.
x-green-arrow-year-one: Andy Diggle and Jock retell Green Arrow’s origin, with Oliver Queen stranded on an island after a betrayal. Read, but I don’t own a copy; the 2027 deluxe edition is on my wishlist.
x-batman-superman-world-s-finest-the-del: Mark Waid and Dan Mora continue Batman and Superman’s partnership in connected adventures across the DC Universe. Collects Batman/Superman: World’s Finest #12–24. Read after Vol. 1, which I own; scheduled for March 9, 2027.
x-green-arrow-year-one-the-deluxe-editio: Andy Diggle and Jock retell Green Arrow’s origin, with Oliver Queen learning to survive with a bow. Collects Green Arrow: Year One #1–6. I’ve read the story; this edition is scheduled for March 23, 2027.
x-the-green-lantern-by-grant-morrison-an: Grant Morrison and Liam Sharp turn Green Lantern into surreal science fiction, with Hal Jordan investigating strange crimes across the cosmos. Collects The Green Lantern #1–12, Season Two #1–12 and Blackstars #1–3. Scheduled for May 11, 2027.
